stories.summary: Ukraine has launched a significant drone attack involving over 1,000 drones targeting Russia, marking the largest assault on Moscow to date. The attack coincided with the final day of tightly controlled parliamentary elections in Russia. Reports indicate that the assault resulted in damage to an oil refinery and a residential building, with at least two fatalities confirmed in Moscow. The mayor of Moscow described the event as the largest drone attack on the city.

stories.title: Pakistan Claims Airstrikes in Afghanistan Kill 28 Militants; Afghanistan Reports Civilian Casualties
stories.summary: Pakistan reported that airstrikes in Afghanistan resulted in the deaths of 28 militants in the border provinces of Kunar and Paktika. In contrast, Afghan authorities stated that three civilians were killed in the strikes. This incident follows a recent attack on police in Kohat, Pakistan.
stories.event_title: Pakistan Storm

story_report.summary: Pakistan said it killed 28 militants in airstrikes in Afghanistan’s Kunar and Paktika provinces, describing the targets as militant sites. Afghan authorities reported three civilian deaths, while the UN mission in Afghanistan said at least three civilians — a man, woman and girl — were killed and four people injured in apparent strikes in Kunar. Afghanistan summoned Pakistan’s chargé d’affaires and lodged a protest, as both sides signaled no immediate easing of tensions.

stories.title: Putin's United Russia Party Secures Majority in Parliamentary Elections
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin's ruling United Russia party has achieved a record majority in the recent parliamentary elections, winning approximately 58% of the vote. The elections, which have faced criticism for being tightly controlled, resulted in United Russia securing 355 out of 450 seats in the Duma. Additionally, 49 veterans of the Ukraine war were elected to the new parliament, further consolidating the party's influence.

story_report.summary: Near-complete results in Russia’s parliamentary election put Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party at about 57.8% of the vote and projected it to win 355 of the 450 seats in the State Duma. The total would exceed the party’s previous high of 343 seats in 2016, consolidating its parliamentary dominance. Officials also said 49 people who participated in the war against Ukraine were elected to the new chamber.

stories.title: UK Charges Man with Genocide-Related Offences from Rwanda
stories.summary: Vincent Brown, also known as Vincent Bajinya, has been charged in the UK with one offence related to genocide and six offences related to murder as a crime against humanity. The 65-year-old is set to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court to face these charges, marking the first prosecution in the UK connected to the 1994 Rwanda genocide.
stories.event_title: UK Charges Man with Genocide-Related Offences from Rwanda

story_report.summary: UK prosecutors have charged Vincent Brown with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six counts of conduct ancillary to murder in connection with the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda. The Crown Prosecution Service says the case is the first time the UK has brought charges relating to the genocide. Brown is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 22, 2026, and police say he has been remanded in custody. The allegations have not been tested in court.

stories.title: China Expels Two Senior Military Leaders Amid Anti-Corruption Drive

This action is part of an ongoing anti-corruption campaign within the military. One of the expelled leaders, Zhang Youxia, was the highest-ranked general in the country, serving as a vice chairman on the Central Military Commission.

story_report.summary: China expelled senior generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Communist Party and military service on September 21 after allegations of corruption and disloyalty. Zhang, formerly the senior vice chairman of the Central Military Commission and China’s highest-ranking uniformed officer, and Liu, the Joint Staff Department chief, had already been removed from the state military commission. The expulsions remove two leading officers from their posts, though no successors were named publicly.
